description: Four judges rate six targets: the worked example for the six intraclass correlation forms.

source.authors: Shrout, P. E., & Fleiss, J. L.
source.title: Intraclass correlations: uses in assessing rater reliability
source.table: Table 2, four ratings on six targets (p. 423); Table 3, analysis of variance for ratings (p. 423); Table 4, correlation estimates from six intraclass correlation forms (p. 424)

notes: ratings, expected.meanSquares, expected.df and expected.icc were transcribed from a scan of the published article (Tables 2, 3 and 4).
The same ratings appear as the sf matrix in the R psych ICC documentation and as judges.dta in the Stata icc manual; both agree with Table 2 cell for cell.
expected.reproduction holds the values the Stata manual prints for these data, to 7 decimals. They are a reproduction, not the published values, and are recorded only as a tighter check.

reproductions.name: R package psych, ICC documentation, example matrix sf (the Shrout and Fleiss 1979 data)
StataCorp, Stata Base Reference Manual, Release 19, entry icc (Intraclass correlation coefficients), Examples 1 to 3 on judges.dta, data from Table 2 of Shrout and Fleiss (1979)

layout: targets x judges: one row per target, one column per judge

reproduction.from: Stata Base Reference Manual, Release 19, icc: Example 1 (one-way), Example 2 (two-way random, absolute agreement), Example 3 (two-way mixed, consistency)
